relationship: Advancing the cycle connects each small processor action to visible changes in data and control, helping learners understand how one instruction unfolds across fetch, decode and execute.

learnerLoop.action: Choose a program, predict what will happen, and advance or run the processor cycle.
learnerLoop.modelChange: The instruction progresses and the processor's stored values, active components and data movement change.
learnerLoop.evidence: The current phase, highlighted activity, changing values and explanation reveal what happened and why.
learnerLoop.nextDecision: Explain the observed change, predict the next action, or compare how another program or instruction model behaves.

invariants: Learners can trace an instruction through fetch, decode and execute and relate each phase to the roles of processor components and memory.
Visible evidence remains causally consistent, so learners can explain why values and data movement change.
safeAdaptations: Invent new programs, values, contexts, prediction tasks or debugging challenges that make the cycle meaningful to a particular audience.
Change the pacing, terminology, amount of guidance or way evidence is revealed while keeping cause and consequence traceable.
Use different visual, narrative or interactive representations that deepen comparison between instructions or processor models.
nonGoals: Expanding into advanced processor architecture unless it directly supports understanding the fetch-decode-execute cycle.

task.description: Goal, three example programs and immediate/direct instruction models.
task.visibility: Present in the corresponding simulation or construction state.

controls.description: Advance one micro-operation or run the clock.
controls.visibility: Present in the corresponding simulation or construction state.

model.description: CPU, buses and RAM stay adjacent; clock and phase strip show execution progression.
model.visibility: Present in the corresponding simulation or construction state.

evidence.description: The current micro-operation and explanation sit below the RAM stick; CPU values use passive flat material backgrounds. The clock trace starts clear of HIGH/LOW labels.
evidence.visibility: Present in the corresponding simulation or construction state.

accumulator.domain: Program arithmetic: supplied add yields 13, subtract 12, multiply 12.
accumulator.source: Active program executed through the micro-operation queue.

modes.operand: Immediate operands use CIR; direct addressing fetches operands from memory.
modes.program: Add/store, subtract/store and multiplication by repeated addition.
modes.support: No Working or assessed exam-level toggle; the instruction-model menu changes the machine trace.

dependencies: Changing program or instruction model resets CPU and memory.
Decode schedules the instruction-specific execution transfers.
implementation.completion: STOP halts and disables further stepping/running until reset.
limitations: Each teaching tick is a micro-operation rather than a literal physical clock-cycle implementation.
